Subject: Post-call exec recap: Redwood Inference & AuroraMed - next steps

Hi Susan / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick executive recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment across teams.

Key business goals we heard:
- Reduce per-interaction latency for clinical triage workflows from ~1.2s to <400ms (avg).
- Cut inference costs ~40% for high-volume chart summarization to support scaling to 3x monthly volume.
- Ensure data separation and auditability to meet health-data compliance for pilots and eventual production.

Top pain points:
- Current vendor struggles with consistent latency under burst loads (esp. mornings).
- Lack of token-level cost visibility and no easy way to route requests between regional capacity.
- Procurement/legal need SOC2 evidence and a clear procurement path we can follow.

Proposed business outcomes (what success looks like over 3-6 months):
1) Pilot with 2 key EMR workflows (triage + discharge summary) meeting 95th percentile latency SLA of <600ms.
2) Unit cost reduction targets and visibility integrated into the dashboard for clinical ops.
3) Signed procurement SLA and rollout plan for Dedicated capacity in region us-west.

Risks / open items:
- SOC2 evidence and data residency controls (AuroraMed legal/procurement review).
- Procurement timeline: need clarity on their internal approval cadence (SOW, PO timing).
- Exec sponsor confirmation for go/no-go at end of pilot.

Immediate next steps:
- Marissa/Redwood: provide SOC2 summary and initial SOW draft by EOD Tue (attached: SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf; SOW draft to follow).
- AuroraMed: confirm procurement contact and earliest available leadership slot for a 30-min alignment call (target week of Mar 29).
- Redwood/Aditya: prepare performance plan & cost estimate for pilot (will include batching/quantization options).

Attachments: AuroraMed_requirements_summary.pdf, SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf

If that matches your view, Susan, we'll get the SOW over and loop in legal/procurement.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Forwarding the recap + attachments and answering the two questions from Susan:

1) Preliminary TCO for 3-month pilot (approx 1M tokens/day):
- Hosted API baseline (burst-capable): ~ $62k/month estimated token cost + infra => ~ $190k for 3 months.
- Dedicated reserved capacity (pilot config): estimated ~ $115k/month (incl. reserved GPU pools + support) => ~ $345k for 3 months, with predictable throughput and lower latency.
- Notes: intelligent batching and KV caching we discussed can reduce effective token spend by 20-30% depending on prompt reuse; we'll model both conservative and optimistic scenarios in the cost deck.

2) Data residency: Redwood can provision pilot capacity in us-west region and a Private deployment if required. For pilot we recommend VPC-dedicated endpoints with KMS-integrated keys; we'll include required controls in the SOW.

Action items I'm taking now (internal):
- Aditya: please prepare the perf plan and conservative/optimistic cost scenarios (deliverable: Mar 26 EOD).
- Laura: draft SOW v1 and capture procurement questions for legal review (deliverable: Mar 25 EOD).

Procurement / AuroraMed: please confirm the PO process and any standard SLA clauses you require so we can bake them into SOW.

Attaching: SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf

Thanks, I'll send SOW v1 once Laura sends initial draft.

Marissa
